purpose: Reviewed allowlist of every line by which the composed production Firestore Rules on gameplay/recovery-v1 differ from what production main deploys. The main gate must see exactly these changes and nothing else. Regenerate only with node tests/support/composed-production-rules.cjs --print-main-delta origin/main, then review every hunk.

candidate.base: main b41f296 (r75, same composed Rules as the r67 pin) plus the owner-decided career start marker: accounts/{uid}/careerStart/current, get/create/update by the owner on an active device, created once from careerIndex/current, then only active may change; list and delete false; plus the Terminal Close stale-write gate: terminal progress, terminal rivalry close and atomic session close take their CAS revision step as a ternary condition after their existing cheap checks, so a stale write is refused at once (no outcome changes)

added: // Stale-write gate (both managers save the same Terminal Close step at once). After the cheap checks that every
// other write path already fails on, the CAS revision step is the condition of a ternary: a write built on a
// revision the document already left is refused right there, and an evaluation pass that cannot read the stored
// document stops there too instead of running the whole check into the 1,000-expression limit. The step stays
// required inside ssjrTerminalFinalEnvelopeCas, so no outcome changes; only the refusal comes sooner.
hunks.why: Terminal Close stale-write gate, comment only: when both managers save the same step at once, the losing write is refused by its CAS revision step before the rest of the check, so the refusal is a plain denial, not the 1,000-expression limit.

Terminal progress update: after the unchanged cheap checks (rivalry id, both states active), the CAS revision step becomes the condition of a ternary in front of the unchanged progress check. The step is still required inside ssjrTerminalFinalEnvelopeCas, so the allow/deny outcome is unchanged; a stale write is just refused at once.

Closes the progress-update ternary: the unchanged progress check, else false. The step is still required inside ssjrTerminalFinalEnvelopeCas, so the allow/deny outcome is unchanged; a stale write is just refused at once.

Atomic session close: after the unchanged state == closed and parent-close-requested checks, the CAS revision step becomes the condition of a ternary in front of the unchanged session-close check. The step is still required inside ssjrTerminalFinalEnvelopeCas, so the allow/deny outcome is unchanged; a stale write is just refused at once.

Closes the session-close ternary: the unchanged session-close check, else false. The step is still required inside ssjrTerminalFinalEnvelopeCas, so the allow/deny outcome is unchanged; a stale write is just refused at once.

Terminal rivalry close: after the unchanged cheap checks (rivalry id, signed in, active to closed), the CAS revision step becomes the condition of a ternary in front of the unchanged close check. The step is still required inside ssjrTerminalFinalEnvelopeCas, so the allow/deny outcome is unchanged; a stale write is just refused at once.

Closes the rivalry-close ternary: the unchanged close check, else false. The step is still required inside ssjrTerminalFinalEnvelopeCas, so the allow/deny outcome is unchanged; a stale write is just refused at once.

added: // CMS_CAREER_START (owner decision): own-account "real career starts here" marker. Created once, active,
// naming exactly the account's career index head ids (none when no index exists; never over sealed pages).
// Afterwards only `active` may change, by CAS. Get, create and update only; no list, no delete.
hunks.why: Career start marker functions, placed after the G-7 career index functions they build on (cmsCareerIndexPageCapacity, careerIndex/current): exact two-key data, create only active with exactly the index head ids (empty when no index, refused over sealed pages), update by CAS changing only active.

Career start marker match: owner-only get of current while the account is active; create and update only through the functions above (active device); list and delete false. No existing rule changes meaning.
